title: CTS Christian Education — Unit 3: Jesus — The Master Teacher

blocks.en: Christian Education — Unit 3: Jesus — The Master Teacher
blocks.es_reference: Educación Cristiana — Unidad 3: Jesús — El Maestro de Maestros

blocks.en: The voice in this unit is Andi's, drawn from her contribution to WiseSpeak (1993). She turns now to the Teacher whose example informs the six characteristics of Unit 2: Jesus.
blocks.es_reference: La voz en esta unidad es la de Andi, extraída de su contribución a WiseSpeak (1993). Ella se vuelve ahora al Maestro cuyo ejemplo informa las seis características de la Unidad 2: Jesús.

blocks.en: Unit 3 · John 13:13–15 · The Model
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 3 · Juan 13:13–15 · El Modelo

blocks.en: Jesus — The Master Teacher
blocks.es_reference: Jesús — El Maestro de Maestros

blocks.en: "I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you."
blocks.es_reference: «Os he dado ejemplo, para que como yo os he hecho, vosotros también hagáis».

blocks.en: Unit Scripture: "You call Me Teacher and Lord, and you say well, for so I am. If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you." — John 13:13–15 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Escritura de la Unidad: «Vosotros me llamáis Maestro, y Señor; y decís bien, porque lo soy. Pues si yo, el Señor y el Maestro, he lavado vuestros pies, vosotros también debéis lavaros los pies los unos a los otros. Porque ejemplo os he dado, para que como yo os he hecho, vosotros también hagáis». — Juan 13:13–15 (RVG)

blocks.en: Orientation: The Master and the Model
blocks.es_reference: Orientación: El Maestro y el Modelo

blocks.en: Jesus called himself the Master Teacher. "You call Me Teacher and Lord, and you say well, for so I am" (John 13:13). He did not flinch from the title. He claimed it. And then he gave the disciples the only definition of "Teacher" that the New Testament will accept: "I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you" (John 13:15).
blocks.es_reference: Jesús se llamó a sí mismo el Maestro de Maestros. «Vosotros me llamáis Maestro, y Señor; y decís bien, porque lo soy» (Juan 13:13). No se retrajo del título. Lo reclamó. Y luego les dio a los discípulos la única definición de «Maestro» que el Nuevo Testamento aceptará: «Ejemplo os he dado, para que como yo os he hecho, vosotros también hagáis» (Juan 13:15).

blocks.en: The Master Teacher does not float above his students. He gives them an example. He does what he asks them to do, and he asks them to do what he has already done. He teaches by being.
blocks.es_reference: El Maestro de Maestros no flota por encima de sus estudiantes. Les da ejemplo. Hace lo que les pide hacer, y les pide hacer lo que ya ha hecho. Enseña siendo.

blocks.en: In Unit 2 we listed six characteristics of the Christian Education teacher. In Unit 3 we will see those same six characteristics in the only Teacher who possessed them all without exception. Jesus was a person of God. Jesus was a student of the Word. Jesus was a servant. Jesus was a student of his students. Jesus was a master of the teaching process. Jesus was a person of prayer. Take any of those six and trace it through the Gospels, and you will find Jesus on every page.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 2 enumeramos seis características del maestro de Educación Cristiana. En la Unidad 3 veremos esas mismas seis características en el único Maestro que las poseía todas sin excepción. Jesús fue una persona de Dios. Jesús fue un estudiante de la Palabra. Jesús fue un siervo. Jesús fue un estudiante de sus estudiantes. Jesús fue un maestro del proceso de enseñanza. Jesús fue una persona de oración. Tome cualquiera de las seis y trácela a través de los Evangelios, y encontrará a Jesús en cada página.

blocks.en: The six characteristics of Unit 2 are not theory. They are a portrait of Jesus.
blocks.es_reference: Las seis características de la Unidad 2 no son teoría. Son un retrato de Jesús.

blocks.en: This unit takes them in the same order. We will end where we began — not behind a lectern, but at the feet of the Master, where every Christian Education teacher learns to teach.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad las toma en el mismo orden. Terminaremos donde comenzamos — no detrás de un atril, sino a los pies del Maestro, donde cada maestro de Educación Cristiana aprende a enseñar.

blocks.en: I. A Person of God: Thirty Years Before the First Sermon
blocks.es_reference: I. Una persona de Dios: Treinta años antes del primer sermón

blocks.en: Luke gives us only one window into the boyhood of Jesus, and it tells us everything we need to know about his preparation for the teaching ministry. Jesus was twelve years old. The family had gone up to Jerusalem for the Passover. When his parents began the journey home, Jesus stayed behind in the temple. Three days later they found him — "sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions" (Luke 2:46). When Mary scolded him, he answered with his first recorded words in Scripture: "Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?" (Luke 2:49).
blocks.es_reference: Lucas nos da una sola ventana a la niñez de Jesús, y nos dice todo lo que necesitamos saber acerca de su preparación para el ministerio de enseñanza. Jesús tenía doce años. La familia había subido a Jerusalén para la Pascua. Cuando sus padres comenzaron el viaje de regreso, Jesús se quedó atrás en el templo. Tres días después lo encontraron — «sentado en medio de los doctores, oyéndoles y preguntándoles» (Lucas 2:46). Cuando María lo regañó, Él respondió con sus primeras palabras registradas en la Escritura: «¿Cómo es que me buscabais? ¿No sabíais que en los negocios de mi Padre me es necesario estar?» (Lucas 2:49).

blocks.en: Eighteen years would pass before Jesus stood up to teach in public. Eighteen years between the question in the temple and the sermon in Nazareth. We do not know exactly what Jesus did during those eighteen years. We know he worked in the carpenter shop. We know he was subject to his earthly parents. We know he "increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man" (Luke 2:52). The Master Teacher did not begin his public ministry until thirty years of private fellowship with the Father had filled his soul to overflowing.
blocks.es_reference: Pasarían dieciocho años antes de que Jesús se levantara a enseñar en público. Dieciocho años entre la pregunta en el templo y el sermón en Nazaret. No sabemos exactamente lo que Jesús hizo durante esos dieciocho años. Sabemos que trabajaba en el taller de carpintero. Sabemos que estaba sujeto a sus padres terrenales. Sabemos que «crecía en sabiduría y en estatura, y en gracia para con Dios y los hombres» (Lucas 2:52). El Maestro de Maestros no comenzó su ministerio público hasta que treinta años de comunión privada con el Padre habían llenado su alma hasta rebosar.

blocks.en: The lesson for the Christian Education teacher is plain. Jesus did not rush. Jesus did not improvise. Jesus did not teach out of an empty cup. He spent thirty years filling the cup before he ever poured a drop into the cup of another. The teacher who tries to skip the filling will find himself dry within a few months. The teacher who is filling now — in the carpenter shop, in the kitchen, in the morning quiet — will have something to pour for the rest of his teaching life.
blocks.es_reference: La lección para el maestro de Educación Cristiana es clara. Jesús no se apresuró. Jesús no improvisó. Jesús no enseñó de una taza vacía. Pasó treinta años llenando la taza antes de jamás verter una gota en la taza de otro. El maestro que trata de saltarse el llenado se encontrará seco en unos pocos meses. El maestro que está llenándose ahora — en el taller de carpintero, en la cocina, en el silencio de la mañana — tendrá algo que verter por el resto de su vida de enseñanza.

blocks.en: II. A Student of the Word: "It Is Written"
blocks.es_reference: II. Un estudiante de la Palabra: «Escrito está»

blocks.en: The Master Teacher's relationship with Scripture was tested in the most public possible way at the very start of his ministry. Forty days in the wilderness, forty days without food, and the Devil himself came to the weakened Christ to tempt him. Three temptations came; three answers were given. Each answer began with the same three words: "It is written" (Matthew 4:4, 7, 10). Each quotation came from the same book of the Old Testament: Deuteronomy.
blocks.es_reference: La relación del Maestro de Maestros con la Escritura fue probada de la manera más pública posible al comienzo mismo de su ministerio. Cuarenta días en el desierto, cuarenta días sin comida, y el Diablo mismo vino al Cristo debilitado para tentarlo. Tres tentaciones vinieron; tres respuestas se dieron. Cada respuesta comenzó con las mismas dos palabras: «Escrito está» (Mateo 4:4, 7, 10). Cada cita vino del mismo libro del Antiguo Testamento: Deuteronomio.

blocks.en: Notice what Jesus did not do. He did not argue with the Devil. He did not negotiate. He did not improvise a clever original answer. He drew from a deep well of memorized, internalized Scripture, and he answered every temptation with what God had already said. The Devil left him. The Master Teacher had won the first battle of his public ministry without saying a single original word.
blocks.es_reference: Note lo que Jesús no hizo. No discutió con el Diablo. No negoció. No improvisó una respuesta original e ingeniosa. Sacó de un profundo pozo de Escritura memorizada e interiorizada, y respondió a cada tentación con lo que Dios ya había dicho. El Diablo lo dejó. El Maestro de Maestros había ganado la primera batalla de su ministerio público sin decir una sola palabra original.

blocks.en: This is the pattern of his entire teaching career. Jesus quoted the Old Testament more than ninety times in the four Gospels. He quoted from the Law, from the Prophets, and from the Psalms. He quoted to teach (Matthew 5), to rebuke (Matthew 22), to defend his ministry (Luke 4), to interpret his own death (Luke 22). He even quoted Scripture from the cross (Matthew 27:46, quoting Psalm 22:1). The Master Teacher's lips were full of the Word of God because the Master Teacher's heart was full of the Word of God.
blocks.es_reference: Este es el patrón de toda su carrera de enseñanza. Jesús citó el Antiguo Testamento más de noventa veces en los cuatro Evangelios. Citó de la Ley, de los Profetas, y de los Salmos. Citó para enseñar (Mateo 5), para reprender (Mateo 22), para defender su ministerio (Lucas 4), para interpretar su propia muerte (Lucas 22). Incluso citó la Escritura desde la cruz (Mateo 27:46, citando el Salmo 22:1). Los labios del Maestro de Maestros estaban llenos de la Palabra de Dios porque el corazón del Maestro de Maestros estaba lleno de la Palabra de Dios.

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher who is not in the Word himself cannot teach the Word to others. He will be reduced, as Andi said in Unit 2, to teaching opinions about the Bible. Jesus modeled the alternative. Know the Word so well that when the test comes — whether the test is a temptation, a hard question from a student, a heresy from a stranger, or a sorrow at midnight — the answer that comes first to the lips is, "It is written."
blocks.es_reference: El maestro de Educación Cristiana que no está en la Palabra él mismo no puede enseñar la Palabra a otros. Se verá reducido, como dijo Andi en la Unidad 2, a enseñar opiniones sobre la Biblia. Jesús modeló la alternativa. Conozca la Palabra tan bien que cuando llegue la prueba — sea una tentación, una pregunta difícil de un estudiante, una herejía de un extraño, o una tristeza a medianoche — la respuesta que primero venga a los labios sea: «Escrito está».

blocks.en: III. A Servant: The Towel and the Basin
blocks.es_reference: III. Un siervo: La toalla y el lebrillo

blocks.en: The most famous teaching moment in the upper room was not a sermon. Jesus did not stand. He stooped. He laid aside his garments, took a towel, and girded himself. He poured water into a basin. And then the Master of the universe knelt at the feet of fishermen and tax collectors and a man who would betray him in less than three hours, and he began to wash their feet (John 13:4–5).
blocks.es_reference: El momento de enseñanza más famoso en el aposento alto no fue un sermón. Jesús no se puso de pie. Se inclinó. Se quitó su manto, tomó una toalla, y se la ciñó. Echó agua en un lebrillo. Y luego el Maestro del universo se arrodilló a los pies de pescadores y publicanos y un hombre que lo traicionaría en menos de tres horas, y comenzó a lavarles los pies (Juan 13:4–5).

blocks.en: The disciples never forgot that lesson. They never forgot that the Master became the slave. Years later, when Peter wrote his first letter, he reached for the same image and told elders to "feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind; neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock" (1 Peter 5:2–3). Peter learned that from a Master who had washed his feet.
blocks.es_reference: Los discípulos nunca olvidaron esa lección. Nunca olvidaron que el Maestro se hizo siervo. Años después, cuando Pedro escribió su primera carta, alcanzó la misma imagen y les dijo a los ancianos que «apacentaseis la grey de Dios que está entre vosotros, cuidando de ella, no por fuerza, sino voluntariamente; no por ganancias deshonestas, sino con ánimo pronto; y no como teniendo señorío sobre la heredad de Dios, sino siendo ejemplos de la grey» (1 Pedro 5:2–3). Pedro aprendió eso de un Maestro que le había lavado los pies.

blocks.en: The Master Teacher's heart for service is seen most clearly in the smallest learners. When the disciples tried to send the children away — "thinking, perhaps, the great Teacher had no time for them," as one writer put it — Jesus was "much displeased" and said, "Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God" (Mark 10:14). Then he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them. The Master of the universe held a four-year-old in his lap. The Christian Education teacher who will not kneel at a child's eye level has not yet understood the kind of Master he serves.
blocks.es_reference: El corazón del Maestro de Maestros por el servicio se ve más claramente en los aprendices más pequeños. Cuando los discípulos trataron de echar a los niños — «pensando, quizás, que el gran Maestro no tenía tiempo para ellos», como dijo un escritor — Jesús se «indignó mucho» y dijo: «Dejad a los niños venir a mí, y no se lo impidáis; porque de los tales es el reino de Dios» (Marcos 10:14). Luego los tomó en sus brazos, puso las manos sobre ellos, y los bendijo. El Maestro del universo sostuvo a un niño de cuatro años en su regazo. El maestro de Educación Cristiana que no se arrodillará a la altura de los ojos de un niño aún no ha comprendido la clase de Maestro a quien sirve.

blocks.en: A teacher who will not serve cannot teach. A teacher who will serve can teach almost anything. Jesus modeled both: real authority and real service, in the same person, on the same evening, with the same towel.
blocks.es_reference: Un maestro que no sirve no puede enseñar. Un maestro que sí sirve puede enseñar casi cualquier cosa. Jesús modeló ambas: autoridad real y servicio real, en la misma persona, en la misma noche, con la misma toalla.

blocks.en: IV. A Student of His Students: The Woman at the Well
blocks.es_reference: IV. Un estudiante de sus estudiantes: La mujer en el pozo

blocks.en: If you want to see the Master Teacher's pedagogical genius in a single lesson, study John 4. Jesus is sitting at a well in Samaria. It is noon. A woman comes alone to draw water. Everything about that picture tells the careful reader that Jesus had already studied his student before he opened his mouth.
blocks.es_reference: Si quiere ver la genialidad pedagógica del Maestro de Maestros en una sola lección, estudie Juan 4. Jesús está sentado en un pozo en Samaria. Es mediodía. Una mujer viene sola a sacar agua. Todo en esa imagen le dice al lector cuidadoso que Jesús ya había estudiado a su estudiante antes de abrir la boca.

blocks.en: He knew her culture. She was a Samaritan, and the Jews "have no dealings with the Samaritans" (John 4:9). He knew her gender. No respectable rabbi would speak to a strange woman alone at a well. He knew her hour. Women drew water in the cool of the morning or the evening, in groups, with conversation. A woman who came at noon, alone, was a woman who had been driven out of the morning crowd. He knew her history before she said a word about it: five husbands, and the man she was now living with was not her husband (John 4:18). And he knew her spiritual longing — she was waiting for the Messiah, even though she did not know she was speaking to him (John 4:25).
blocks.es_reference: Conocía su cultura. Ella era samaritana, y los judíos «no se tratan con los samaritanos» (Juan 4:9). Conocía su género. Ningún rabino respetable hablaría con una mujer extraña sola en un pozo. Conocía su hora. Las mujeres sacaban agua en el frescor de la mañana o de la tarde, en grupos, con conversación. Una mujer que venía a mediodía, sola, era una mujer que había sido expulsada de la multitud de la mañana. Conocía su historia antes de que ella dijera una palabra al respecto: cinco maridos, y el hombre con quien ahora vivía no era su marido (Juan 4:18). Y conocía su anhelo espiritual — estaba esperando al Mesías, aunque no sabía que estaba hablando con él (Juan 4:25).

blocks.en: And so the Master Teacher did not begin with a sermon. He did not begin with a verse. He began with a request: "Give me to drink" (John 4:7). He met her where she was, with what she had, in the role she was already playing. From there he moved her, step by step, from physical water to living water, from her need to her sin, from her sin to the Messiah. By the end of the conversation, she left her waterpot at the well and ran into the city saying, "Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?" (John 4:29).
blocks.es_reference: Y así el Maestro de Maestros no comenzó con un sermón. No comenzó con un versículo. Comenzó con una petición: «Dame de beber» (Juan 4:7). La encontró donde estaba, con lo que tenía, en el papel que ya estaba desempeñando. Desde ahí la movió, paso a paso, del agua física al agua viva, de su necesidad a su pecado, de su pecado al Mesías. Al final de la conversación, ella dejó su cántaro en el pozo y corrió a la ciudad diciendo: «Venid, ved a un hombre que me ha dicho todo cuanto he hecho. ¿No será éste el Cristo?» (Juan 4:29).

blocks.en: Jesus taught one Samaritan woman so well because Jesus had first studied that one Samaritan woman. The Christian Education teacher does the same work with every learner who walks into the classroom. Know the student's culture. Know the student's age and stage. Know the questions the student brings, and the questions the student cannot quite ask. Then meet the student there, with what the student already has, in the role the student is already playing. The teaching that begins with the student is the teaching that ends with the student running into the city to tell others.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús enseñó a una mujer samaritana tan bien porque Jesús primero había estudiado a esa mujer samaritana. El maestro de Educación Cristiana hace la misma obra con cada aprendiz que entra al aula. Conozca la cultura del estudiante. Conozca la edad y la etapa del estudiante. Conozca las preguntas que el estudiante trae, y las preguntas que el estudiante no puede formular del todo. Luego encuéntrese con el estudiante allí, con lo que el estudiante ya tiene, en el papel que el estudiante ya está desempeñando. La enseñanza que comienza con el estudiante es la enseñanza que termina con el estudiante corriendo a la ciudad a contarles a otros.

blocks.en: V. A Master of the Teaching Process: Every Method, Used Well
blocks.es_reference: V. Un maestro del proceso de enseñanza: Cada método, bien usado

blocks.en: The Master Teacher used every method known to good teaching. He used the lecture — the Sermon on the Mount is three chapters long. He used questions — over three hundred of them are recorded in the four Gospels. He used parables — more than forty stories from the everyday life of his hearers. He used object lessons — a child set in the midst (Mark 9:36), a coin produced from the mouth of a fish (Matthew 17:27), a fig tree withered in the morning (Mark 11:20), water turned to wine (John 2). He used demonstration — he washed feet, he broke bread, he wept at a tomb. He used field trips — he took the disciples up the mountain, across the sea, through the grain fields, into the temple courts.
blocks.es_reference: El Maestro de Maestros usó cada método conocido de la buena enseñanza. Usó la conferencia — el Sermón del Monte tiene tres capítulos. Usó preguntas — más de trescientas están registradas en los cuatro Evangelios. Usó parábolas — más de cuarenta historias de la vida cotidiana de sus oyentes. Usó lecciones objetivas — un niño puesto en medio (Marcos 9:36), una moneda sacada de la boca de un pez (Mateo 17:27), una higuera secada en la mañana (Marcos 11:20), agua convertida en vino (Juan 2). Usó la demostración — lavó pies, partió pan, lloró ante una tumba. Usó viajes — llevó a los discípulos al monte, al otro lado del mar, por los sembrados, a los atrios del templo.

blocks.en: And he used different group sizes for different purposes. He preached to crowds of five thousand (Matthew 14). He taught the Twelve in private (Mark 4:34). He had inner-circle moments with three (Peter, James, and John). He had one-on-one conversations with Nicodemus at night (John 3) and with the woman at the well at noon (John 4). The Master Teacher fitted the method to the moment and the audience.
blocks.es_reference: Y usó diferentes tamaños de grupo para diferentes propósitos. Predicó a multitudes de cinco mil (Mateo 14). Enseñó a los Doce en privado (Marcos 4:34). Tuvo momentos de círculo íntimo con tres (Pedro, Jacobo, y Juan). Tuvo conversaciones uno a uno con Nicodemo de noche (Juan 3) y con la mujer en el pozo a mediodía (Juan 4). El Maestro de Maestros ajustó el método al momento y a la audiencia.

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher who limits himself to one method is limiting Jesus. A teacher who only lectures has not yet imitated the Master who told stories. A teacher who only tells stories has not yet imitated the Master who asked sharp questions. A teacher who only asks questions has not yet imitated the Master who sometimes simply showed his disciples how to do something and let them imitate. The classroom is a place for many methods, varied as the Master Teacher varied them, suited each Sunday morning to the lesson and the learner.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro de Educación Cristiana que se limita a un solo método está limitando a Jesús. Un maestro que sólo da conferencia aún no ha imitado al Maestro que contaba historias. Un maestro que sólo cuenta historias aún no ha imitado al Maestro que hacía preguntas penetrantes. Un maestro que sólo hace preguntas aún no ha imitado al Maestro que a veces simplemente les mostraba a sus discípulos cómo hacer algo y les permitía imitar. El aula es un lugar para muchos métodos, variados como el Maestro de Maestros los varió, adaptados cada domingo por la mañana a la lección y al aprendiz.

blocks.en: Units 6 through 9 of this course will unfold the methods one by one — lesson planning and aims, methods and strategies, questioning and case study and experiential study, Bible learning activities. Each unit exists because the Master Teacher used the method, and we are still learning how to use it after him.
blocks.es_reference: Las Unidades 6 a 9 de este curso desplegarán los métodos uno por uno — el plan de lección y los objetivos, los métodos y estrategias, la pregunta y el estudio de caso y el estudio experiencial, las actividades de aprendizaje bíblico. Cada unidad existe porque el Maestro de Maestros usó el método, y todavía estamos aprendiendo a usarlo después de él.

blocks.en: VI. A Person of Prayer: The Solitary Place Before Dawn
blocks.es_reference: VI. Una persona de oración: El lugar solitario antes del amanecer

blocks.en: Mark records a single quiet sentence that ought to undo every busy teacher: "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed" (Mark 1:35). The night before had been a long one. Jesus had healed the sick at sundown until late. The disciples were sleeping. The Master Teacher was praying.
blocks.es_reference: Marcos registra una sola oración silenciosa que debería deshacer a cada maestro ocupado: «Y levantándose muy de mañana, mucho antes de amanecer, salió y se fue a un lugar desierto, y allí oraba» (Marcos 1:35). La noche anterior había sido larga. Jesús había sanado a los enfermos al atardecer hasta tarde. Los discípulos dormían. El Maestro de Maestros oraba.

blocks.en: This was not a one-time event. It was the rhythm of his life. Before he chose the Twelve — the most consequential teaching decision of his ministry — he "continued all night in prayer to God" (Luke 6:12). Before the cross, he prayed in Gethsemane until "His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down to the ground" (Luke 22:44). When the crowds pressed him so hard he could not eat, Luke says, "He Himself often withdrew into the wilderness and prayed" (Luke 5:16). The busier he got, the more he prayed.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no fue un evento único. Era el ritmo de su vida. Antes de escoger a los Doce — la decisión de enseñanza más consecuente de su ministerio — «pasó la noche orando a Dios» (Lucas 6:12). Antes de la cruz, oró en Getsemaní hasta que «su sudor era como grandes gotas de sangre que caían hasta la tierra» (Lucas 22:44). Cuando las multitudes lo presionaban tanto que no podía comer, Lucas dice: «Él se apartaba a los desiertos, y oraba» (Lucas 5:16). Mientras más ocupado se ponía, más oraba.

blocks.en: The teacher who does not pray relies on himself, as Andi warned in Unit 2. The teacher who prays relies on the One who breathed the Scriptures, who set the lesson before the lesson plan, and who knows each student by name. Jesus's teaching was bathed in prayer because Jesus's life was bathed in prayer. The teacher who prays as Jesus prayed will, in time, teach as Jesus taught.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro que no ora se apoya en sí mismo, como advirtió Andi en la Unidad 2. El maestro que ora se apoya en Aquel que respiró las Escrituras, que estableció la lección antes del plan de lección, y que conoce a cada estudiante por nombre. La enseñanza de Jesús estaba bañada en oración porque la vida de Jesús estaba bañada en oración. El maestro que ora como Jesús oró, con el tiempo, enseñará como Jesús enseñó.

blocks.en: Notice what the Master Teacher does NOT pray for. He does not pray for a bigger crowd. He does not pray for a better classroom. He does not pray for a different student. He prays for the Father's will, for the disciples by name, for the unity of those who would believe through their word (John 17). The Christian Education teacher learns from him how to pray, as well as how to teach.
blocks.es_reference: Note por lo que el Maestro de Maestros NO ora. No ora por una multitud más grande. No ora por una aula mejor. No ora por un estudiante diferente. Ora por la voluntad del Padre, por los discípulos por nombre, por la unidad de los que creerían por la palabra de ellos (Juan 17). El maestro de Educación Cristiana aprende de él cómo orar, así como cómo enseñar.

blocks.en: Closing: Sit at His Feet
blocks.es_reference: Cierre: Siéntese a Sus pies

blocks.en: Luke 10 tells of two sisters in Bethany. Martha was busy serving. Mary "sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word" (Luke 10:39). When Martha complained, Jesus answered, "But one thing is needed, and Mary has chosen that good part, which will not be taken away from her" (Luke 10:42).
blocks.es_reference: Lucas 10 cuenta de dos hermanas en Betania. Marta estaba ocupada sirviendo. María «sentada a los pies de Jesús, oía su palabra» (Lucas 10:39). Cuando Marta se quejó, Jesús respondió: «Pero una cosa es necesaria; y María ha escogido la buena parte, la cual no le será quitada» (Lucas 10:42).

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher's first place is not behind a lectern. It is at the feet of the Master Teacher, hearing his word, before ever attempting to pass that word on to anyone else. Six characteristics of the teacher: a person of God, a student of the Word, a servant, a student of the students, a master of the teaching process, a person of prayer. Six characteristics in Jesus, perfectly embodied. Sit at his feet, and you will learn how to teach.
blocks.es_reference: El primer lugar del maestro de Educación Cristiana no es detrás de un atril. Es a los pies del Maestro de Maestros, oyendo su palabra, antes de jamás intentar pasar esa palabra a otra persona. Seis características del maestro: una persona de Dios, un estudiante de la Palabra, un siervo, un estudiante de los estudiantes, un maestro del proceso de enseñanza, una persona de oración. Seis características en Jesús, perfectamente encarnadas. Siéntese a sus pies, y aprenderá cómo enseñar.

blocks.en: The teacher who never sits at his feet will eventually have nothing to give. The teacher who sits there often will never run out.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro que nunca se sienta a sus pies eventualmente no tendrá nada que dar. El maestro que se sienta allí a menudo nunca se quedará sin nada.

blocks.en: In Unit 4 we will turn from the Master Teacher to the learners. We will discover, as Jesus did at every well and on every roadside, that the learner is not a problem to be managed but a person to be loved. The teacher who has sat at the Master's feet is the teacher who can love a learner the way the Master loved that woman in Samaria at high noon.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 4 nos volveremos del Maestro de Maestros a los aprendices. Descubriremos, como Jesús lo descubrió en cada pozo y en cada camino, que el aprendiz no es un problema que manejar sino una persona que amar. El maestro que se ha sentado a los pies del Maestro es el maestro que puede amar a un aprendiz de la manera en que el Maestro amó a esa mujer en Samaria en pleno mediodía.

mc.stem: What is the anchor scripture for Unit 3?
mc.why: John 13:13-15 anchors this unit because Jesus himself claims the title 'Teacher' and immediately defines it: 'I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you.' The Master Teacher teaches by being.

mc.stem: What was Jesus doing at age twelve when his parents found him in the temple?
options: Sitting among the doctors, hearing them and asking them questions
Reading prophecies aloud to the crowd
mc.why: Luke 2:46 describes Jesus 'sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.' Even at twelve, he was already doing two of the master teacher's signature moves: listening and asking.

mc.stem: How did Jesus answer each of the Devil's three temptations in the wilderness?
options: With 'It is written' followed by Scripture from Deuteronomy
mc.why: Each of Jesus's three answers in Matthew 4 began with 'It is written' and quoted Deuteronomy. The Master Teacher did not improvise; he drew from a deep well of memorized, internalized Scripture.

mc.stem: Approximately how many times did Jesus quote the Old Testament in the four Gospels?
mc.why: Jesus quoted the Old Testament more than 90 times across the four Gospels, drawing from the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms. His teaching was saturated with the Word he himself had inspired.

mc.stem: What did Jesus do for the disciples in the upper room before the Last Supper?
mc.why: In John 13:4-5, Jesus laid aside his garments, took a towel, poured water into a basin, and washed the disciples' feet. The Master became the slave to teach his students what greatness looks like in his kingdom.

mc.stem: What did Jesus say after washing the disciples' feet (John 13:15)?
options: "I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you"
mc.why: This is the explicit definition of 'Master' that Jesus gives in the upper room. The Master Teacher does not float above his students; he gives them an example. He teaches by being.

mc.stem: What was Jesus's response when the disciples tried to send the children away?
options: He agreed they were too young to learn
He sent them to John the Baptist instead
He was much displeased and said 'Suffer the little children to come unto me'
He told the parents to come back later
mc.why: In Mark 10:14, Jesus was 'much displeased' and said, 'Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.' The Master of the universe held a four-year-old in his lap. The Christian Education teacher who will not kneel at a child's eye level has not yet understood the kind of Master he serves.

mc.stem: Where did Jesus meet the Samaritan woman, and at what time of day?
options: At the temple, in the morning
At a marketplace, in the evening
At a synagogue, on the Sabbath
mc.why: John 4 records that Jesus sat at Jacob's well at the sixth hour (noon). Everything about that picture — the hour, the woman alone, the foreign territory — tells the careful reader that Jesus had already studied his student before he opened his mouth.

mc.stem: How did Jesus begin his conversation with the woman at the well?
options: With a request: "Give me to drink"
With a parable about a wedding
mc.why: In John 4:7, Jesus's first words were 'Give me to drink.' He did not begin with a sermon or a verse. He met her where she was, in the role she was already playing, with what she already had.

mc.stem: Approximately how many parables did Jesus tell that are recorded in the Gospels?
mc.why: More than 40 parables are recorded in the Gospels, all drawn from the everyday life of Jesus's hearers: farming, fishing, weddings, lost coins, lost sons. The Master Teacher fitted his stories to his students.

mc.stem: Approximately how many questions did Jesus ask that are recorded in the four Gospels?
mc.why: The Gospels record more than 300 questions from Jesus. He used questions to teach, to convict, to draw out faith, to expose hypocrisy, and to lead his students to discover truth for themselves.

mc.stem: What does Mark 1:35 say Jesus did 'a great while before day' after a long night of healing?
options: Departed into a solitary place and prayed
mc.why: Mark 1:35: 'And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.' The night before had been long; the disciples were sleeping; the Master Teacher was praying. The busier he got, the more he prayed.

mc.stem: How long did Jesus pray before choosing the Twelve (Luke 6:12)?
mc.why: Luke 6:12 says Jesus 'continued all night in prayer to God' before choosing the Twelve. The most consequential teaching decision of his ministry was preceded by an entire night in prayer.

mc.stem: Where did Jesus pray before the cross, until his sweat became as great drops of blood?
mc.why: Luke 22:44 records Jesus praying in Gethsemane until his sweat 'was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.' The Master Teacher's life was bathed in prayer at every critical moment, including the night before he died.

mc.stem: Of whom does Luke 10:39 say she 'sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word'?
mc.why: Mary of Bethany (Lazarus's sister), in contrast to her busy sister Martha. Jesus said she had chosen 'that good part, which shall not be taken away.' The Christian Education teacher's first place is at the Master Teacher's feet.

mc.stem: How are the six characteristics of Unit 2 related to Jesus, according to Andi?
options: They are general principles that loosely apply
They are theory; Jesus is the perfect embodiment
They were derived from secular education
They apply to children but not to Jesus
mc.why: The orientation states it explicitly: 'The six characteristics of Unit 2 are not theory. They are a portrait of Jesus.' Each characteristic finds its perfect example in him.

mc.stem: How long did Jesus prepare in private before beginning his public ministry?
mc.why: Jesus did not begin his public ministry until age thirty, after thirty years of private fellowship with the Father in the home, the carpenter shop, and the synagogue. The teacher who tries to skip the filling will find himself dry within a few months.

mc.stem: Which teaching method did Jesus NOT use, according to Section V?
options: He used every method known to good teaching
mc.why: The Master Teacher used every method — lecture, questions, parables, object lessons, demonstration, field trips, and varied group sizes. The teacher who limits himself to one method is limiting Jesus.

mc.stem: What did Jesus call himself in John 13:13?
mc.why: In John 13:13, Jesus said, 'You call Me Teacher and Lord, and you say well, for so I am.' He claimed both titles. Then he immediately defined them by washing the disciples' feet — real authority paired with real service.

mc.stem: According to the closing, where is the Christian Education teacher's first place?
options: At the feet of the Master Teacher, hearing his word
mc.why: Andi quotes Mary of Bethany at Jesus's feet (Luke 10:39) as the model. The teacher's first place is not behind a lectern but at the Master Teacher's feet, hearing his word, before ever attempting to pass that word on to anyone else.
